tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H45): GEMM2 phase rebuild in tc_kernel: SM-filling unit tables, TMA bulk-reduce epilogue, one-MMA [h|g]. Rows: 2,768 / 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 / 8,384 / 16,384 (tc_kernel only; sc rows unchanged). STEP 0 (<=10 min): read the parent card first (what r10 shipped: balanced tables, g or no g, B-scale, KS per row). Run cuobjdump -res-usage on the parent build and record STACK for every tc/sc instantiation (must be 0). Unless the parent card records it done, also run the barrier safety check (audit item 5): protocol review of release/acquire plus fence.proxy.async before any TMA read of data other CTAs wrote with generic stores, and a 1500-call stress loop at 8,768 and 16,384 checked against the torch reference within tolerance. On any failure, revert to cg grid.sync and report. STEP 1: stamp the parent's GEMM2 phase at 8,768, 16,768, 32,768 and 16,384: sync-2 release, first MMA, per-stage time, mainloop end, red.add drain end, units per CTA, busy CTAs. STEP 2 (10-min probe): 148 CTAs, each reduces a 25 KB fp32 smem tile [128 ch][49 tok] (and [128][196]) into a contiguous NCHW fp32 array after the 2xL2 flush. Compare cp.reduce.async.bulk.global.shared::cta.bulk_group.add.f32 (one per image segment, elected thread, commit/wait_group) against the coalesced scalar red.add form. Confirm that ptxas accepts the f32 form on sm_100a, check correctness, and record the time. STEP 3, build: (a) a bulk-reduce epilogue that drains TMEM to smem as dense [c][HW] per image segment and issues one bulk add per segment (prefill out = x + b2' unchanged; handle segments at N padding; wait_group before exit). (b) Per-row unit tables so GEMM2 units are 144-148 (raise KS where units < 120; atomics no longer scale per element). (c) Only if the parent still runs two accumulators with 2N <= 256: land the h and g boxes in adjacent 64-token chunks of one B stage and issue one MMA at 2N (I19). Add (a), (b), (c) one at a time and stamp after each. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 including portal-order re-runs. Run harness_time interleaved x3 against the parent on the six rows. Check STACK on the shipped build. Precision: only the fp32 summation order of split-K changes, so cite the r8 log plus a single-seed fp64 check per row; if (c) or any B-scale arithmetic changes roundings, log 10 rounds per row. Success: GEMM2 phase (sync-2 release to last CTA exit) at least 40 % shorter on >= 4 of 6 rows. Rows faster than the parent, interleaved x3: 32,768 by >= 4 us, 16,768 and 16,384 by >= 3, 8,768 by >= 2.5, 8,384 by >= 2, 2,768 by >= 1.5. 16/16 pass, STACK 0. Refuted if: The bulk reduce is < 1.3x faster than scalar red.add in STEP 2 AND the shipped build is within 1 us of the parent on >= 4 of 6 rows; or the STEP 1 stamps show the drain is < 1.5 us on every row and filling the SMs gives < 1 us. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid or cluster barrier counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

Experiment E2 (tests H44): Weight path off the critical path: bulk-copy W pass at DRAM rate, in-ring W1 conversion where slices are shared. Rows: 2,768 / 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 (C=768). Apply to 8,384 / 16,384 only if they gain. STEP 0: read the parent card. Record cuobjdump STACK for the parent and for every build you time. STEP 1: stamp parent phase A at 8,768 and 32,768: W1 issue end, plane copies landed, conv end, W1 conversion end, phase-A end median/max, sync-1 release, plus GEMM1 end, which shows the cost of the deferred W2 pass. STEP 2, variant A (bulk weight pass): replace the 12 LDG.128 per lane W1 stream with cp.async.bulk fp32 chunks (>= 32 KB per CTA per chunk, double-buffered in smem that the conv planes leave free; plane copies stay first) using an L2::cache_hint evict_first policy on the reads. Do the LN-weight fold, the row sums u and cvt.rn.f16x2 from smem on all warps, and write fp16 rows by cp.async.bulk store or STG.128 with evict_last (own buffers only, no applypriority). Treat the deferred W2 pass the same way. Target: the W1 stream at >= 6.5 TB/s and sync 1 >= 1.5 us earlier. STEP 3, variant B gate (<= 15 min): microbench with 96 CTAs: 12 stages of fp32 TMA boxes [128 hidden x 64 k] with a FLOAT32 map, feeding 4 converter warps (no LDG in flight; fold, cvt, write the SW128 K-major fp16 A stage, fence.proxy.async, arrive), feeding the MMA warp at N=98/112 against the same B. Compare per-stage clk with the fp16 ring (~480 clk). Build in-ring W1 only if the gate is <= 1.25x, and only for rows where >= 4 token tiles share each W1 slice (8,768, 16,768, 32,768). Never at 2,768, where first-touch DRAM at 40 GB/s/SM per slice loses. W2 stays in the deferred pass. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 and harness_time interleaved x3 against the parent. Precision: if fp16(lnw*W1), u and the conversion lane order are unchanged, cite the log plus a single-seed check per row. If the u summation order changes, run a 10-round fp64 log on the C=768 rows. Success: Sync-1 release >= 2 us earlier at 8,768 and 32,768 (stamps). Rows >= 2 us faster than the parent at 2,768 / 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768, interleaved x3. 16/16 pass, STACK 0. Refuted if: Variant A runs the W1 stream below 5.5 TB/s, or moves sync 1 by < 1 us, AND the variant B gate exceeds 1.25x; or every shipped row is within 1 us of the parent. Experiment E3 (tests H46): New lineage J: cluster split-K cells for the low-M wide-C rows (2,768 and 8,768). From scratch (you may copy the r0 baseline's binding glue). The kernel is a specialist for C=768, HW=49, B in {2, 8}; every other row may fall back to the r0 anchor so that all 16 workloads pass (the merge takes only rows that win). Use the notebook recipes: bulk-plane conv with LN partial statistics; the LN fold z = rs*(acc - mu*u) + v with u = row sums of fp16(lnw*W1) and v = W1.lnb + b1; tcgen05 kind::f16 swap-AB descriptors (K-major SW128 A box SBO 1024 +32 B per k16; MN-major SW128 B LBO 8192 SBO 1024 +2048 per k16; idesc bits); whole-warp TMA and MMA roles with elect.sync; cooperative launch combined with a cluster attribute via cudaLaunchKernelExC; CUTLASS-style release plus ld.acquire + fence.proxy.async for TMA readers; A&S erfc GELU; b2' = W2.gb + b2 kept in fp32; GRN via h and g = gw*gf*h with two GEMM2 accumulators (gf is complete inside a cell that covers whole images); a self-resetting scratch counter. Validate the engine against torch before anything else. STEP 0 gate (<= 15 min): (a) cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters at 512 thr and your smem size for cluster sizes 3, 4, 6 and 8. The grid must be co-resident with >= 144 CTAs. (b) Exchange microbench after the 2xL2 flush: each CTA holds a 128 x N fp32 partial (N=98: 50 KB; N=196: 100 KB). The owner of 128/KS rows sums them over KS cluster mates by three routes: L2 scratch with barrier.cluster arrive.release / wait.acquire and LDG.128; DSMEM ld.shared::cluster; cp.reduce.async.bulk .add.f32 into an L2 fp32 buffer plus a cluster barrier. Record the time per CTA. Kill the lineage's build if the best route takes > 1.5 us at 50 KB. STEP 1, build: phase A (conv, LN stats, W1/W2 fp16 conversion, out prefill if your GEMM2 scheme needs it). Sync 1. GEMM1 cells: 2,768 = 24 hidden tiles x 1 token group (98 tokens) x KS 6; 8,768 = 24 x 2 groups of 196 tokens (N=208, MMA at ideal) x KS 3; or whatever STEP 0a allows. Exchange, then the owner does fold, GELU, per-(image,k) sumsq, staged coalesced h/g stores, and a red.add of the per-image gf sum. Sync 2. GEMM2 cells: (128-channel out tile, token group, K slice). Reduce inside the cluster first, so at most one add per output element per cluster reaches out (bulk reduce into the prefilled out, or a plain store x + b2' + sum when one cluster covers all of K). Never rely on the harness zero-filling the outputs. STEP 2: stamps (sync 1, GEMM1 mainloop end, exchange end, epilogue end, sync 2, GEMM2 end). Then run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs, and harness_time interleaved x3 against r10-merge at 2,768 and 8,768. Check cuobjdump STACK = 0. Precision: new summation order; log 10 rounds of fp64 reference on both rows (max |err| and beyond-own-atol count). Success: 2,768 <= 19 us and 8,768 <= 25 us rented, or >= 15 % faster than r10-merge interleaved on both rows; 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-atol elements, STACK 0. Incubation line: within 10 % of r10-merge on at least one of the two rows. Refuted if: The STEP 0 exchange takes > 1.5 us per CTA by every route, or fewer than 120 CTAs can be co-resident in clusters of >= 3; or the built kernel's GEMM1 phase (sync-1 release to GEMM1 end) is not >= 30 % shorter than D's stamped 11.7 us at 8,768. Experiment E4 (tests H47): New lineage K: persistent warp-specialised tcgen05 engine with epilogue/mainloop overlap for the multi-tile wide-C rows. From scratch (you may copy the r0 baseline's binding glue). The kernel is a specialist for 32,768 and 16,768 (C=768, HW=49) and 16,384 (C=384, HW=196), with 8,384 as a stretch; other rows fall back to the r0 anchor. Notebook recipes: bulk-plane conv, LN fold, descriptors, cta_group::2 syntax (whole kernel one cta_group), coop + cluster launch, one producer warp per stage, A&S erfc GELU, staged coalesced h stores, GRN via two accumulators or in-smem B scale. STEP 0 (<= 20 min): (a) audit item 2: straight-line unrolled issue of 64 MMAs with precomputed descriptors at N = 64 / 128 / 224 / 256, 1 vs 128 CTAs, 1SM M=128 vs pair M=256, smem-resident operands; record clk per instruction. Choose tile N and pair mode from this. (b) Overlap gate: one CTA per SM (148), 512 threads; the MMA warp runs a 12-stage mainloop into accumulator 1 while 12-14 epilogue warps drain accumulator 0 (tcgen05.ld, LN fold, A&S GELU, sumsq, fp16 staged stores). Measure epilogue elements/us/SM and MMA stage clk with and without the other running. Gate: both keep >= 80 % of their solo rate. If the gate fails, stop building and report the limiter (issue slots, TMEM ld port, smem bandwidth). Optional, if >= 3 B200 min remain: the I4 microbench (A from TMEM vs SW128 smem at N=64). STEP 1, build one cooperative launch with fixed roles: warp 0 TMA, warp 1 MMA (uniform loop, elect.sync), the rest epilogue. Two TMEM accumulators of <= 256 columns. Balanced static per-CTA tile lists over (hidden tile, token range) with N >= 196, multiples of 74 pairs if paired. GEMM1: phase A (conv, weights), sync, then for each tile run the mainloop of tile i+1 while the epilogue warps finish tile i. Sync 2. GEMM2 with the same engine: units balanced to 148, the epilogue of unit i overlapped with the mainloop of unit i+1, coalesced or bulk-reduce adds into the prefilled out. STEP 2: stamps per phase, then run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs, and harness_time interleaved x3 against r10-merge on the three rows. Check cuobjdump STACK = 0. Precision: log 10 rounds of fp64 reference on every shipped row (a B-scaled GEMM2 is the twice-rounded class). Success: 32,768 <= 50, 16,768 <= 36, 16,384 <= 41 us rented, or >= 15 % faster than r10-merge interleaved on >= 2 of the 3 rows; GEMM1 phase <= 14 us at 32,768. 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-atol, STACK 0. Incubation line: within 10 % of r10-merge on one row with the overlap gate passed. Refuted if: The STEP 0b overlap gate fails (either side < 80 % of its solo rate); or the built kernel's GEMM1 phase at 32,768 is not >= 30 % shorter than D's stamped ~28 us (sync 1 ~9 to G1 end 37-39 us).
